fields.title: قلعہ العقیر
fields.summary: بندرگاہ کی نگہبانی کرتا ایک تاریخی قلعہ، جو العقیر کی پرانی تجارتی خوش حالی کا گواہ ہے۔
fields.body: قلعہ العقیر خلیج کے ساحل پر، الاحساء کے مشرق میں، العقیر کی تاریخی بندرگاہ کی عمارتوں کے درمیان واقع ہے۔ یہ بندرگاہ سعودی عرب کے مشرقی ساحل کی پہلی سمندری بندرگاہ ہے، اور پرانے زمانے میں یہ سمندر کی طرف نجد کا دروازہ تھی۔ یہاں سے ملنے والے آثار قدیمہ گواہی دیتے ہیں کہ اس جگہ تجارت نہایت قدیم زمانے سے ہوتی رہی تھی۔ آج جو عمارتیں دکھائی دیتی ہیں ان میں قلعہ، سرائے، دار الامارہ، چنگی خانہ اور مسجد شامل ہیں۔ اسی بندرگاہ پر 1341 ہجری (1922 عیسوی) میں سرحدوں کے تعین کے لیے معاہدہ العقیر پر دستخط ہوئے۔ بیسویں صدی عیسوی کے وسط میں دمام کی بندرگاہ قائم ہوئی تو العقیر کی بندرگاہ کی اہمیت گھٹ گئی، اور اس کی عمارتیں ایک پورے دور کی گواہ بن کر رہ گئیں۔ 1990 کی دہائی کے اواخر میں ان کی مرمت ہوئی۔ اس مقام پر مرمت کا کام جاری ہے، اور ممکن ہے کہ اس کے کچھ حصے بند ہوں۔
fields.area: العقیر کی بندرگاہ، الاحساء کے مشرق میں خلیج کے ساحل پر

practical.label: اوقات
practical.value: باہر سے دیکھا جا سکتا ہے

accuracy.why: 'Since the fifteenth century' follows the English with its calendar word and nothing computed («پندرہویں صدی عیسوی سے»); both superlatives stand under 'one of' («قدیم ترین اور مشہور ترین مساجد میں سے ایک») and 'the oldest quarter' as the Arabic carries it; 'around' before 850 AH and before 1,600; a working mosque said three times at one strength and no visiting time anywhere; the summary's era is the Arabic's own phrase («بنو جبر کی ریاست کے دور کی»); the minaret is still a cylinder, in plain words («گول ستون کی شکل کا»); the row's «تقدس» is the source's 'sanctity'. Three points off: the visiting row asks («پہن کر آئیں», «خیال رکھیں») where the source says 'with' (the shared row); 'a beacon' is a centre («مرکز»); and the remedies of round 1 drop the English's 'living' and the Arabic's connective and say 'old' for 'historic' («پرانے ہفوف»).

nativeness.why: «آباد مسجد» is right for both readers, and round 1's «درس و تدریس اور علم کا مرکز» and «اصل تعمیراتی مواد برتا گیا» passed the second. What he misread is answered: the set phrase for an age of tyranny is broken up by the body's own phrase, the roofs no longer send him to the prayer niche, the rolling pin is gone in his own words, and the semicolons of the page are stops. Four points off: roofs that cut one another still cannot be pictured («ایک دوسرے کو کاٹتی قوس نما چھتیں»: the source's 'intersecting vaults'); «ساتر لباس» is a word of the fiqh books to him (kept, on an even count of four readers); «منصوبے کے تحت» and three superlatives in two sentences are the source's; and six edits in three leaves are unread — «قوس نما» is the judge's own word, and the row is the sister judge's wording, which no reader has seen.

compliance.why: «مسجد الجبری» feminine throughout («بنی ہے», «رہی», «کھلی ہے»); «بنو جبر کی ریاست» in summary and body, the name never straight before the word for an era; «سیف بن زامل الجبری» with its article; «تقریباً 1,600» grouped as the English groups it; the visiting row equal to jawatha-mosque's byte for byte, a stop inside and none at the end; the programme unmarked; no U+061B. Two points off: «بنو جبر» and the programme are pending, and the six edits are unproofed.

fit.why: For a Muslim family this is the page of the five that sits closest to home. Two points off: «زیارت» and «زائرین» carry the sense of a shrine for both readers of this batch (ruled for every mosque page on the two readers of the sister batch, who accept the word); the request to dress modestly and to respect «اس مقام» reads to both as written for someone who has never entered a mosque. That the page talks of a fee twice and says nothing of when to come or of women is the source's.

structure.why: Eleven leaves in pack order; three card rows by their ids; the label «زیارت» without stop or bracket; the area line leads with the larger place as a bare name (ruling P20); no hours row is invented where the source has none; the stop inside the visiting row is not a final one (ruling P26).

fields.title: مسجد الجبری
fields.summary: محلہ الکوت میں بنو جبر کی ریاست کے دور کی ایک مسجد، جسے پندرہویں صدی عیسوی سے نمازیوں نے آباد رکھا ہے۔
fields.body: مسجد الجبری محلہ الکوت میں قصر ابراہیم کے قریب واقع ہے۔ الکوت پرانے ہفوف کا قدیم ترین محلہ ہے۔ یہ مسجد الاحساء کی قدیم ترین اور مشہور ترین مساجد میں سے ایک ہے۔ اسے سیف بن زامل الجبری نے بنو جبر کی ریاست کے دور میں، تقریباً 850 ہجری (1446 عیسوی) میں تعمیر کیا اور اس کے لیے کھیت اور کھجور کے باغ وقف کیے۔ یہ عبادت کے ساتھ ساتھ درس و تدریس اور علم کا مرکز بھی رہی۔ یہ مٹی اور چونے کے پتھر سے بنی ہے۔ ایک دوسرے کو کاٹتی قوس نما چھتیں، کئی برآمدے اور مختلف وضع کے گنبد اس کی پہچان ہیں، اور اس کا مینار گول ستون کی شکل کا ہے۔ اس میں تقریباً 1,600 نمازیوں کی گنجائش ہے۔ صدیوں کے دوران اس کی بار بار مرمت ہوئی۔ آخری مرمت 1437 ہجری (2016 عیسوی) میں تاریخی مساجد کی دیکھ بھال کے منصوبے کے تحت ہوئی، اور اس میں اصل تعمیراتی مواد برتا گیا۔ یہ آج بھی ایک آباد مسجد ہے۔

practical.label: داخلہ
practical.value: آباد مسجد، داخلے کی کوئی فیس نہیں

practical.label: زیارت
practical.value: زائرین کے لیے کھلی ہے۔ ساتر لباس پہن کر آئیں اور اس مقام کے تقدس کا خیال رکھیں

blind_reader_rulings.reason: Applied for the half that is the Urdu's: «کے کنارے» is «کے سرے پر» in the summary, his own wording, so that an unknown name is no longer followed by the word for a bank or shore. The first reader misread the same word the same way (his observation 9); two of two. The other half is the source's and stays: neither language says what Al-Mubarraz is, and 'north of' is not put in the summary's place, where both sources say 'on the edge of'.

His sentence, word for word: a comma after the name. The seam was opened by round 1, when the bracket between the two names went; the proof pass found it too (its finding 1), and b1's judge wrote the rider to item N14 on it.

CONFIRMED from the pack, and now by two readers of two: this page's sources say 'Saud bin Abdulaziz (later Imam)' («الإمام لاحقاً») and nothing more; that 'Imam' is here a ruler's title is said on the khuzam page only ('third imam of the First Saudi State'). The Urdu says what each page says. His remedy, the identification of the other page, would bring a statement of another page into this one: logged, with a one-line option for the owner («جو بعد میں اسی ریاست کے امام بنے»). Harm: both readers took the builder for a man who later became a mosque's imam or a religious leader.
His order, word for word: «دو منزلہ ایک گول برج ہے». Round 1's wording was the first reader's own and failed with the second; this one keeps what each of them asked for.

Applied with his second remedy, word for word, in place of the judge's own sentence of round 1. Not applied: dropping the sentence. That the same fact stands three times on a short page is the source's ('a small watch-and-guard fort' in the summary and in the body, then 'a lookout post').

«نقشہ» is the word of both sources ('it follows a square plan', «على مخطط مربع») and his «مربع شکل کا» would say the shape and drop the plan: content of the field's source for a smoother register (ruling P24). The first reader read the sentence and held it up as the measure he wanted on the other page (his observation 22). One reader of two, minor; kept and charged under nativeness. On record for the owner: «یہ مربع شکل کا ہے، تقریباً بیس میٹر لمبا اور اتنا ہی چوڑا».

The word says what the source says: 'falling out of use'. The dictionary's first sense of «متروک» is 'left, given up' (Rekhta entry page, read in this round: «جسے چھوڑ دیا جائے، چھوڑا ہوا، ترک کردہ»), and the reference site writes «متروک عمارت» of a disused building (4 pages). His «خالی چھوڑے جانے سے پہلے» says 'left empty', which is another thing. The first reader read the word and quoted it without a remark. That the page does not say when the fort was given up or whether it is shut today is the source's.

CONFIRMED from the pack again, by a second reader: the only hours are those of 'the garden and walkway', 'Free entry' does not say to what, and nothing says whether the fort is entered. Nothing is supplied. What he made of it: 'I can plan an evening walk; I cannot tell my children whether they will get into the fort.'

Two source nouns, two Urdu words: the body's 'a green park' («منتزه») is «تفریح گاہ» and the card's 'the garden and walkway' («الحديقة والممشى») is «باغ اور چہل قدمی کا راستہ». Neither language says they are one place; the first reader asked the same (his observation 14).

Which fairs and in what season: neither source names or dates the 'festival seasons'. His second point is not applied: «ورثے اور فنون کی تقریبات» is 'heritage and arts events' in the site's own word for heritage (the ruled «ورثہ» of «عالمی ورثہ»); his «ثقافتی اور فنی تقریبات» says 'cultural' where both sources say heritage («تراثية»). The first reader read the phrase without a remark. Round 1's «میلے لگتے ہیں» passed him: no 'miles'.

CONFIRMED from the pack: the derivation is the source's as it stands, and the Urdu carries exactly what it says. English: 'its name derives from the zimam, the rein by which camels are led'; Arabic: the name is 'from' the word «الزمام», «الذي تُقاد به الإبل». Neither gives a bridge between the fort's name and the word it names; the Urdu quotes the word the source quotes and gives the source's own explanation, nothing more and nothing less. The first reader stopped at the same place (his observation 19, moderate); two of two, and this one calls it an error in the place's own name. Nothing may be supplied from outside the page. For the owner, read in this round on the Arabic reference site (not a source of the site, not used in the Urdu): its article on this fort says that the name goes back to the Arabic word that is the fort's own name, which means the rein that leads a camel and is tied in its nose — the bridge the site's sentence leaves out. Harm: 'as it stands the derivation does not follow, and it made me doubt the page.'

CONFIRMED from the pack, as in round 1: the body says 'restored and opened to visitors in 2017', the only card row says 'currently closed for restoration and heritage development', and the summary says nothing of a closure; the owner confirmed on 2026-10-12 that the fort is closed and that both statements stand. The Urdu carries both at the source's strength with no word between them, and the status row is untouched. Two readers of two set out for the fort on the strength of the body: 'I had already decided to go. Then the card says it is closed … I came away thinking the paragraph is out of date.' Closed since when, until when, and whether the outside can be seen meanwhile are in no source.

The status row is the site's own statement, confirmed by the owner, and it stays exactly as it is, the status first: a reader's rewording of it goes to the owner (ruling P25). Both readers have now written the reason first and faulted «ورثے کی ترقی» ('office language'; 'not an Urdu expression'), and both reach for «ترقیاتی کام». His wording also drops 'heritage', which is the source's. Two one-line options for the owner, both with every word of the source: the row with the everyday adjective, status first — «فی الحال بند ہے، مرمت اور ورثے کے ترقیاتی کاموں کی وجہ سے» (stage 1's recorded alternative) — and the same in Urdu order, «مرمت اور ورثے کے ترقیاتی کاموں کی وجہ سے فی الحال بند ہے». Kept, and charged under nativeness.

The template prints the component number bare after the badge label in every language. Readers of all three batches of the round have taken it for a year, a code or, here, a phone extension. Recorded for the interface batch; nothing in the page fields may explain it.

Applied for the two things that are the Urdu's, by item N16 as b1's judge amended it in round 2 on this very observation and on its own reader's: no quotation marks and no «مقام» before the property's name, in the summary and in the body (changes k-unesco-summary and k-unesco-body); the wording is sahood's. Not applied: «یونیسکو کی عالمی ورثے کی فہرست» — this page's sources say 'UNESCO-listed' and 'inscribed by UNESCO' and never name the list (the first reader asked the same); and that a fort is one of twelve parts of an oasis is the source's vocabulary. What passed him: the inscription in a sentence of its own.
His sentence, word for word, with both commas. As observation 2.

That the towers guard the wall is the image of both sources ('is guarded by six towers', «تحرسه ستة أبراج»), kept by the Russian and German lines and by b1's sahood; his remedy, the first reader's too («اس پر چھ برج ہیں»), drops it (ruling P24). Two readers of two now hear it as a turn of another language, both minor: kept and charged under nativeness, with their wording on record as an option for the owner. Round 1's «مخروطی شکل کے ہیں» is in his own remedy.

No gloss stands in a title or a summary (P3c as amended, point 1; P3c-labels), and the name is built from its Arabic spelling (rulings P1, P17). The gloss stands where the ruling puts it, at the first mention in the body, and he calls it good. The first reader made the same remark; recorded in the entry.

The page never says who King Abdulaziz is, in either language (stage 3 was tempted to add it and held back). The name is the verified entry; its note has recorded since stage 4 that a reader from the subcontinent thinks first of the Delhi scholar, and he says the year and the place correct it at once.

The two main points are the source's, now from two readers: nothing says whether this man is the builder's son or a later descendant (the house was built 65 years before he was born), and the bracket '(1853–1921)' is unlabelled and Gregorian only in both languages. The third point is the Urdu's and is answered: «جو» after «گھر رہا،» pointed at the house for a moment; the clause is a sentence now («وہ … تھے»).

The summary and the body say the same thing in almost the same words because both sources do, and 'the Saudi state' beside 'the modern Saudi state' is theirs. The summary is two sentences where the English has one long one with a dash; it is the longest summary of the five in the source too.

His wording, word for word. Round 1 refused the first reader's same remark under ruling P25; with two readers and a remedy that leaves the claim as flat and as strong as it was, the refusal no longer holds. «الاحساء» still stands in the sentence so that the pronoun cannot point at the state.
Whose guests, and whose clothing and personal effects: the sources say 'sitting areas for guests and displays of clothing and personal effects' and no more. Round 1's «اور یہیں» passed him.
'Historical and explanatory photographs' is all the sources say («صور تاريخية وإرشادية»); the Urdu is word for word. Two readers of two cannot tell what hangs on the wall.

The name is a descriptive rendering of a body no Urdu source names (entry pending), and by item N16 as amended no translated name of a body takes quotation marks; it inflects like any phrase. Read as a description it says the same thing: a Saudi body for antiquities and museums restored the house. Two readers of two cannot tell a name from a description; recorded in the entry. Round 1's «2005 سے 2007 تک» passed him.

The English body is one paragraph and the template renders a non-Arabic body as one block; the Arabic has five paragraphs. He calls the sentences 'plain and mostly good Urdu'. Two readers of two lost their way in the block on a phone.

The heading is the interface string trails.partOf (b0-ui, final), and 'Trails' reads as roads in the English too. Recorded for the interface batch with his wording («یہ مقام سیر کے ان راستوں میں شامل ہے») and his count of three things called «راستہ»; the routes under the heading show as a mark on his page because no trail has an Urdu title yet.

CONFIRMED from the pack, as in round 1: a row labelled 'Hours' that holds a status and no hours, a row that says 'Free entry', and a body that ends 'some parts may be closed' straight after 'restored in the late 1990s'; the template then adds its notice about hours. No reader can tell whether the castle is entered. Round 1's wording of the status did what item N25 meant it to: he read «باہر سے دیکھا جا سکتا ہے» as 'I cannot go in', not as 'open'. His form-only remedy, a status row of its own, is a change to the source's rows and goes to the owner. What he made of it: 'I cannot tell whether we would walk through the buildings or stand at a fence.'
Both sources title the page for the castle and write the body about the port; who built the castle, when, how large it is and what it looks like are in neither language. Two readers of two.

Applied for the half that is the Urdu's: the two look-alike words no longer stand side by side. Urdu has the name of the thing, «دار الامارہ», a reference article and a dictionary headword. Two readers of two and the stage-5 proofreader had stopped at the pair, and round 1 had found no remedy. What the building was beyond that — he asks whether it was a governor's office — is not said by either source.

The owner-ruled wording (build check C34): 'the first seaport', where 'seaport' is the source's own double («ميناء بحري») and 'first' has neither a date nor a sense in either language; it stands in an apposition without a tense, and a past tense in the Urdu would say that the port no longer holds the rank. Four readers of the two attraction batches have now stopped at the line.

Applied, with the proof pass (its finding 2): the trade is in the past now, in his verb and the reference's own frame for a past that finds attest. That «نہایت قدیم زمانے سے» gives no idea of how old is the source's 'remote antiquity'.
Whose borders, and between whom: 'demarcating borders' is all either source says. Round 1's «اسی بندرگاہ پر» passed him.

Three places where both sources say witness or attest («شاهدة», «تشهد», «شاهداً»): one in the summary, two in the body. Cutting one would take its content out of its field (ruling P24). Two readers of two, both minor, and both call the last one good Urdu; kept and logged with the source's repetitions.
His wording, word for word. Round 1's verb was the judge's own and failed with him as the stage-5 verb had failed with the first reader; the noun the two verbs would not fit gives way.

He took the word for the town toll and 'hesitated over whether this is the same thing'; he was not misled. The only everyday word for a customs house is a loan, and a hesitation does not meet the second condition of the loan test (b0-ui, P16-test). The first reader read the word without a remark. The entry stays pending for exactly this sense, with his hesitation recorded.

His wording: the body's own phrase in the summary, «بنو جبر کی ریاست کے دور کی», which is also what the Arabic summary says. The title stays: «مسجد الجبری» is the mosque's reference title, and the article keeps it from being the bare word for 'forced' (item N27). Who the Banu Jabr were beyond a state is not said by the source.

Applied for the one cause he names that is the Urdu's: «محراب دار» sent him to the prayer niche; the roofs are «قوس نما» now. Not answered, and said plainly: he could not picture roofs that cut one another, as the first reader could not; 'intersecting vaults' is the source's phrase and no wording weighed since stage 1 says both of its facts more plainly. Charged under nativeness.
His wording, word for word: «گول ستون کی شکل کا». It says 'cylindrical' in plain words, which the first reader's «گول» did not; two readers of two had smiled at the rolling pin.

The source has both rows in both languages ('Entry: a working mosque, no entry fee'; 'Fees: free entry'). A translation does not merge card rows. Two readers of two find talk of a fee strange on a mosque page.

When a visitor may come, whether between prayers, and whether there is a place for women: in no source; the owner's question on working mosques is open and the Urdu states no time. The label «زیارت» and «زائرین» stay by item N17 (b1 rounds 1 and 2): of the round's four readers of mosque pages the two of b1 accept the word on Jawatha and the two of this batch feel the weight of a shrine on an ordinary working mosque; none offers another label. Charged under fit. The heading «سیاحوں کے لیے معلومات» is the interface's.

Applied as far as the shared row moved: b1's judge amended it in round 2 on its second reader and this one, and the row here is that row byte for byte — a stop for the semicolon, «تقدس» for «حرمت». «ساتر لباس» stays as that batch ruled it, on an even count (the first reader of each batch wrote the word himself, the second of each finds it a word of the fiqh books); the options are on record with b1's entry. «اس مقام» and the request itself are the owner-fixed row; his «مسجد کے احترام» is not taken.

The three superlatives are the source's, each under its own claim ('the oldest quarter', 'one of Al-Ahsa's oldest and most celebrated mosques'), and are not thinned (ruling P25). «پرانے ہفوف» beside «قدیم ترین» is round 1's remedy for «تاریخی ہفوف», which the first reader said Urdu does not say; it is b1's form on ameeriah, read there by two readers. One reader each way; kept.
'Around 850 AH / 1446 CE' is the sources' own pair. Nothing is computed or rounded (b1's item N12). Two readers of two ask whether 'about' covers the bracket.

The template's notice (det.hoursNotice, b0-ui): he calls the wording natural Urdu and misses the means — none of the five pages has an operator link — and the notice stands under cards that show no hours. Recorded for the interface batch; all four readers of the two attraction batches have said it.

The interface string fav.add (b0-ui, final). Recorded for that batch: three of four readers of the attraction batches read it first as 'preserve this place'; he says the phone habit corrects it at once and the confirmation is fine.

Ruling P13 (4), kept by b1's judge in both rounds (item N10): four o'clock is a measured point of the calibration's table and a batch judge does not reopen it. Three readers of four have now said «سہ پہر»; the option is on record for whoever reopens P13: «سہ پہر 4 بجے».

Interface strings of b0-ui (det.nearby.h, det.nearby.d), final. Recorded for that batch: all four readers of the attraction batches hear the line as translated, and this one writes a third remedy («آس پاس کے مقامات، جنہیں آپ اپنی سیر میں شامل کر سکتے ہیں۔»); both second readers call the heading advertisement Urdu.
The accessible name of a photo is built by the template (the title and a number); the attraction files carry no description of a picture. Two readers of two. Recorded for the interface batch.
